content.content: {"result":"{\"success\": true, \"data\": {\"path\": \"/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_14/projects/distill_sparse_swiglu/paper_framing.md\", \"content\": \"# Paper Framing — distill_sparse_swiglu\\n\\n## Target Venue\\n- Primary: EMNLP 2026 Main (ARR May 2026 cycle)\\n- Deadline: 2026-05-25 (ARR submission)\\n- Track: Efficient Methods for NLP\\n\\n## Core Claims\\n\\n1. **KL-trained sparsity predictors eliminate the need for error compensation networks**: At 50% model-level sparsity on SwiGLU LLMs, a KL-trained contextual predictor (no compensation) matches or exceeds BCE+compensation quality (FastForward-style), eliminating 67.2M compensation parameters (~256MB, 32 layers × bottleneck MLP) and per-layer GEMV overhead at inference. All quality comparisons must be presented alongside inference cost (params, FLOPs, latency) to prevent \\\"unfair comparison\\\" attacks. (Headline claim)\\n\\n2. **SPON's static correction is orthogonal to KL and too weak to complement it**: Logit-space decomposition (plan_005) shows SPON's bias correction is near-orthogonal to KL's mask effect (cos_sim=0.196, per-layer ≤0) with only 15.8% relative magnitude. Cross-layer interaction is non-trivial (30.6%) but PPL recovery remains modest (7.3%, 0.23 PPL). Rather than KL \\\"subsuming\\\" SPON, the two target different error components—but SPON's component is too small to provide meaningful complementary benefit. Strengthens Claim 1: static correction is not just redundant but irrelevant to the dominant error mode that KL addresses. (Evidence: plan_005_subsumption_s42, spon_2048_s42, D009, D010)\\n\\n3. **KL advantage grows with sparsity level (testable prediction)**: BCE's per-neuron factorized gradient (mean-field analog) misses joint neuron interactions scaling as O(s^2 D^2). We predict KL-vs-BCE delta follows approximately quadratic curve in sparsity level s — to be validated by 7-level sparsity sweep (plan_008). If empirical scaling deviates from quadratic (linear, log, or phase transition), the actual pattern is itself a finding; abstract/intro will report observed scaling, not assumed quadratic.\\n\\n## Story Spine\\n\\n- **Problem**: SwiGLU activation sparsity enables 40-60% neuron pruning at inference, but training-free heuristics (WINA/TEAL) leave a 6+ point quality gap, while learned BCE predictors require auxiliary compensation networks adding ~256MB overhead (FastForward).\\n\\n- **Existing approaches & gaps**: (a) Training-free (WINA, TEAL, R-Sparse): no training cost, but quality gap too large for deployment. (b) Static learned (SPON): zero-overhead bias correction via KL distillation, but input-independent — cannot adapt to per-input neuron importance. (c) Contextual learned (FastForward): BCE predictor + compensation MLP, near-dense quality but inference overhead from compensation network. Gap: no prior work trains the contextual predictor itself with KL, and no work quantifies how much static correction remains useful once a coupled-loss contextual predictor is in place.\\n\\n- **Our framing / headline question**: \\\"Does output-distribution distillation (KL) make error compensation unnecessary for contextual sparsity prediction?\\\" The theoretical grounding: BCE gradient dL_BCE/ds_j depends only on neuron j (factorized), while KL gradient dL_KL/ds_j couples all active neurons through d_logits/dh * dh/dm — a mathematical property of the gradient structure, not an analogy. This means KL captures joint interaction effects that BCE misses, especially at high sparsity.\\n\\n- **Headline result template**: \\\"On [benchmarks], a KL-trained predictor at 50% model-level sparsity achieves [X] quality (within [Y]% of dense) without compensation, while BCE+compensation achieves [Z] quality but adds 67.2M parameters ([W] ms/token overhead) — demonstrating that output-distribution distillation renders error compensation unnecessary—SPON's residual correction is orthogonal to KL's dominant effect and too weak to complement it—enabling a simpler, lighter inference pipeline with strictly better efficiency-quality tradeoff.\\\"\\n\\n## Two-Dimensional Taxonomy (Conceptual Contribution)\\n\\n|                          | Decomposed (BCE) | Intermediate (MSE) | Coupled (KL) |\\n|--------------------------|:-----------------:|:-------------------:|:-------------:|\\n| Static                   | —                 | —                   | SPON          |\\n| Per-layer                | —                 | ShadowLLM           | —             |\\n| Per-token contextual     | FastForward       | —                   | **Ours**      |\\n\\nPositions prior work and ours on two axes: correction granularity (static -> per-token) x training signal coupling (decomposed/BCE -> coupled/KL). Highlights the empty cell we fill.\\n\\n## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns\\n\\n1. **\\\"Incremental / no new algorithm\\\"**: Mitigate with formal decomposition framework, quantitative s^2 prediction, and comprehensive four-quadrant outcome analysis showing all results are informative.\\n\\n2. **\\\"KL wins only because more compute\\\"**: Addressed by iso-compute ablation (plan_003) giving BCE equivalent total FLOPs via extended training.\\n\\n3. **\\\"Gumbel-sigmoid relaxation, not KL, explains gains\\\"**: Addressed by STE baseline (plan_002) isolating loss function contribution.\\n\\n4. **\\\"Single model / limited generalization\\\"**: Addressed by Mistral-7B-v0.3 validation (plan_009) with different architecture (GQA + sliding window).\\n\\n5. **\\\"Effect size may not hold on downstream tasks\\\"**: Full benchmark suite (PPL + 5 discriminative + LongBench + MT-Bench) covers all axes.\\n\\n6. **\\\"Unfair comparison: BCE+comp close to KL but at higher inference cost\\\"**: All result tables and figures must co-report quality AND inference cost (compensation params, per-token FLOPs, end-to-end latency). Efficiency-accuracy Pareto frontier (plan_007) is the definitive visualization. Even if BCE+comp matches KL on PPL, KL wins on the Pareto frontier — that IS the claim.\\n\\n## Venue Fit\\n- EMNLP Efficient Methods track: strong fit for activation sparsity + distillation\\n- NLP-specific evaluation (LongBench long-context, MT-Bench multi-turn) strengthens EMNLP fit vs pure systems venue\\n- Novelty ceiling acknowledged: contribution is systematic composition + rigorous ablation, not new architecture\\n\", \"total_chars\": 6050, \"truncated\": false}, \"error\": null, \"metadata\": {}}"}

## Target Venue
- Primary: EMNLP 2026 Main (ARR May 2026 cycle)
- Deadline: 2026-05-25 (ARR submission)
- Track: Efficient Methods for NLP

## Core Claims

1. **KL-trained sparsity predictors eliminate the need for error compensation networks**: At 50% model-level sparsity on SwiGLU LLMs, a KL-trained contextual predictor (no compensation) matches or exceeds BCE+compensation quality (FastForward-style), eliminating 67.2M compensation parameters (~256MB, 32 layers × bottleneck MLP) and per-layer GEMV overhead at inference. All quality comparisons must be presented alongside inference cost (params, FLOPs, latency) to prevent "unfair comparison" attacks. (Headline claim)

2. **SPON's static correction is orthogonal to KL and too weak to complement it**: Logit-space decomposition (plan_005) shows SPON's bias correction is near-orthogonal to KL's mask effect (cos_sim=0.196, per-layer ≤0) with only 15.8% relative magnitude. Cross-layer interaction is non-trivial (30.6%) but PPL recovery remains modest (7.3%, 0.23 PPL). Rather than KL "subsuming" SPON, the two target different error components—but SPON's component is too small to provide meaningful complementary benefit. Strengthens Claim 1: static correction is not just redundant but irrelevant to the dominant error mode that KL addresses. (Evidence: plan_005_subsumption_s42, spon_2048_s42, D009, D010)

3. **KL advantage grows with sparsity level (testable prediction)**: BCE's per-neuron factorized gradient (mean-field analog) misses joint neuron interactions scaling as O(s^2 D^2). We predict KL-vs-BCE delta follows approximately quadratic curve in sparsity level s — to be validated by 7-level sparsity sweep (plan_008). If empirical scaling deviates from quadratic (linear, log, or phase transition), the actual pattern is itself a finding; abstract/intro will report observed scaling, not assumed quadratic.

## Story Spine

- **Problem**: SwiGLU activation sparsity enables 40-60% neuron pruning at inference, but training-free heuristics (WINA/TEAL) leave a 6+ point quality gap, while learned BCE predictors require auxiliary compensation networks adding ~256MB overhead (FastForward).

- **Existing approaches & gaps**: (a) Training-free (WINA, TEAL, R-Sparse): no training cost, but quality gap too large for deployment. (b) Static learned (SPON): zero-overhead bias correction via KL distillation, but input-independent — cannot adapt to per-input neuron importance. (c) Contextual learned (FastForward): BCE predictor + compensation MLP, near-dense quality but inference overhead from compensation network. Gap: no prior work trains the contextual predictor itself with KL, and no work quantifies how much static correction remains useful once a coupled-loss contextual predictor is in place.

- **Our framing / headline question**: "Does output-distribution distillation (KL) make error compensation unnecessary for contextual sparsity prediction?" The theoretical grounding: BCE gradient dL_BCE/ds_j depends only on neuron j (factorized), while KL gradient dL_KL/ds_j couples all active neurons through d_logits/dh * dh/dm — a mathematical property of the gradient structure, not an analogy. This means KL captures joint interaction effects that BCE misses, especially at high sparsity.

- **Headline result template**: "On [benchmarks], a KL-trained predictor at 50% model-level sparsity achieves [X] quality (within [Y]% of dense) without compensation, while BCE+compensation achieves [Z] quality but adds 67.2M parameters ([W] ms/token overhead) — demonstrating that output-distribution distillation renders error compensation unnecessary—SPON's residual correction is orthogonal to KL's dominant effect and too weak to complement it—enabling a simpler, lighter inference pipeline with strictly better efficiency-quality tradeoff."

## Two-Dimensional Taxonomy (Conceptual Contribution)

|                          | Decomposed (BCE) | Intermediate (MSE) | Coupled (KL) |
|--------------------------|:-----------------:|:-------------------:|:-------------:|
| Static                   | —                 | —                   | SPON          |
| Per-layer                | —                 | ShadowLLM           | —             |
| Per-token contextual     | FastForward       | —                   | **Ours**      |

Positions prior work and ours on two axes: correction granularity (static -> per-token) x training signal coupling (decomposed/BCE -> coupled/KL). Highlights the empty cell we fill.

## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns

1. **"Incremental / no new algorithm"**: Mitigate with formal decomposition framework, quantitative s^2 prediction, and comprehensive four-quadrant outcome analysis showing all results are informative.

2. **"KL wins only because more compute"**: Addressed by iso-compute ablation (plan_003) giving BCE equivalent total FLOPs via extended training.

3. **"Gumbel-sigmoid relaxation, not KL, explains gains"**: Addressed by STE baseline (plan_002) isolating loss function contribution.

4. **"Single model / limited generalization"**: Addressed by Mistral-7B-v0.3 validation (plan_009) with different architecture (GQA + sliding window).

5. **"Effect size may not hold on downstream tasks"**: Full benchmark suite (PPL + 5 discriminative + LongBench + MT-Bench) covers all axes.

6. **"Unfair comparison: BCE+comp close to KL but at higher inference cost"**: All result tables and figures must co-report quality AND inference cost (compensation params, per-token FLOPs, end-to-end latency). Efficiency-accuracy Pareto frontier (plan_007) is the definitive visualization. Even if BCE+comp matches KL on PPL, KL wins on the Pareto frontier — that IS the claim.

## Venue Fit
- EMNLP Efficient Methods track: strong fit for activation sparsity + distillation
- NLP-specific evaluation (LongBench long-context, MT-Bench multi-turn) strengthens EMNLP fit vs pure systems venue
- Novelty ceiling acknowledged: contribution is systematic composition + rigorous ablation, not new architecture
